Re-posting the same weight adds no entry; a changed weight adds one and kept_precise stays true for auto_photo. 3 new pytest tests pass and the reminder suite passes (11). PASS. (4) HIGH, stitched measurement bias: improved but NOT within 5%. Single-shot fullbody.jpg (re-run today, unchanged) gives chest 75 / waist 64 / hips 87 / shoulder 33 / inseam 78. Stitched gives 81 / 70 / 93 / 37 / 77, i.e. +8%, +9.4%, +6.9%, +12%, -1.3%. Iteration 22 had 69/59/80/30/91, so the bias flipped direction: inseam is now fine but every width is too high. The stitched image is now cropped below the feet: 960x1393 with no white band. PARTIAL FAIL.

minor.issue: test_quick_estimate.py TestQuickEstimateValidation and TestQuickEstimateFlow fail with 403 prelaunch_owner_only, because their throwaway TEST_ users are not in OWNER_EMAILS. This is an environment/test issue, not a regression. Also, test_onboarding_reminder.py and the new weight-history class share user_avatar_test, so they are order-dependent when run in the same pytest session. Run them separately: both pass.

ui_bugs.issue: The stitched body is still about 9-10% too short, so all widths are inflated by 7-12% (shoulder 37 vs 33, chest 81 vs 75, waist 70 vs 64, hips 93 vs 87). Proof: running the single-shot extractBodyRatios on the stitched image gives 81/70/92/37/78, the same as the 2-shot result. So the error is in the stitch geometry, not in the width bands. Ground truth: upper.jpg is fullbody rows 0-744 at scale 1, and lower.jpg is fullbody at 1.2x, rows 500-1196 (fullbody pixels). In the mock both become 1.2x of fullbody, so the correct s is 1.0. Registering the stitched legs against fullbody gives s≈0.91 (legs drawn at about 1.09x instead of 1.2x). The lower photo is also anchored about 46 fullbody px too far down (seam at stitched y≈845), so a band just below the hips is lost under the seam. RCA: hipW() measures the silhouette width at each photo's own MediaPipe hipY. The hip landmark drifts at the frame edges (bottom of photo 1, top of photo 2), so the two widths come from different body heights. On an A-line dress the band in photo 2 sits lower and is wider, so wl is too big and s too small. The vertical anchor u.hipY - l.hipY*s inherits the same landmark drift.

issues: The white band under the feet is fixed (crop at mask bottom + 3%). A slight hip seam remains: skirt step and background edge at about y=845. It is mirrored, which is expected for mirror mode.

action_items: HIGH: make the photo1-to-photo2 registration independent of the hip landmarks. Both photos contain an overlap band (in the test images about fullbody rows 500-744). Register that overlap by image or mask matching: search scale s and offset dy (and dx) to maximise the NCC or IoU of the segmentation mask, or of grayscale, between the bottom ~20% of photo 1 and the top of photo 2. Then use that s/dy both for legLen and for the stitch. A cheaper option: compare the mask-width PROFILES over the whole overlap (many rows) instead of a single ±1.5% band at each photo's own hipY. Validate with upper/lower vs fullbody: the target is chest 75 / waist 64 / hips 87 / shoulder 33 / inseam 78 (±5%).
critical_code_review_comments: pose.js: the `s` fallback u.hipJ / l.hipJ is the method already shown to be unreliable (+17% inseam in iteration 22). Better to fail with a retake code than silently fall back to it.
pose.js: legLen is measured from l.hipY, which is the same drifting landmark. Once a robust overlap registration exists, map u.hipY into photo-2 coordinates and measure from there.
AvatarBox.onCapture now re-fetches /profile/measurements before deciding to ask for body data. This is correct, and it costs one extra GET per capture.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Camera mock: add_init_script overrides navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia to return the canvas.captureStream of a 960x1000 canvas redrawing window.__imgs[window.__cur] (contain-fit, white background) every 50ms. Set __cur='lower' after the first snap. Baseline: getUserMedia rejects, then /settings, avatar-change-btn, set_input_files on avatar-camera-native-input. Ground truth for the images: upper.jpg = fullbody[0:744] at 1x; lower.jpg = fullbody at 1.2x, crop y 600-1435, x 0-960. A useful diagnostic is to download the stitched avatar (GET /api/files/{avatar path}) and push it through the single-shot path, or register it against fullbody with PIL at different scales.
rca of the issue: Stitched widths are inflated because the stitched body is about 10% short: the leg scale s is about 0.91 instead of 1.0, and the lower photo's anchor is offset by about 46 px. Cause: the hip-line silhouette width is sampled at each photo's own MediaPipe hipY. That landmark drifts at the frame edges, so the bands are taken at different body heights (flared dress, so different widths). Fix: register the overlap region between the photos instead of relying on the hip landmark.
